g.text: sd Restaurant Rush - Stage 3: VIP customer C4 during Happy Hour (tag stage-3)
Messages 12-13 go to GameController's current Promotion, which is hh here.
In the [else] branch it is still the starting NoPromotion, which returns 0,
so applyPromotionGoodwill() returns before the loop below.
Use case: the manager plays turns 10 to 13 with C4, a VIP, switches Happy Hour on, and the game is judged after turn 18. Messages are numbered in time order.
[turn = 1 .. config.getMaxTurns() (18 turns; turns 10 to 13 are shown)]
Starting conditions (Stage 3, base setting, seed 42, runs/victory.txt), start of turn 10:
revenue $54.00 from 2 paid customers; C3 is eating at Table 1; Table 2 and the queue are free;
Happy Hour has not been used (promotion = NoPromotion). C4, a VIP, is about to arrive.
Outcome: answering y to Happy Hour on turn 10 changes C4's bill and recorded satisfaction:
the Burger is locked at $15.00 x 0.9 x 0.8 = $10.80 instead of $13.50, and C4 pays at 100, not 95.
The game is a VICTORY either way: 5 paid, $88.80, average 83.6 (with n: $91.50, average 82.6).
Turn 10 Step 1: C4 arrives. Step 2: Happy Hour decision, then Host, Waiter and Chef. Step 5: waiting.
happyHourUsed = true. This manager choice changes C4's outcome:
every order taken while it runs is billed 20% less.
promotion stays NoPromotion, so there is no goodwill, and C4's Burger
would later be billed 1350 ($13.50) instead of 1080 ($10.80).
C4 is waiting but already at 100 (the maximum), so nothing changes yet;
C3 is eating, so it is not awaiting service and receives nothing.
Before each prompt GameController builds the list of legal tasks (legalSeatingCommands,
legalWaiterCommands, legalChefCommands); a staff member whose only task is wait is not asked.
The task is not spent; the loop asks the same staff member again.
The same check-and-retry applies to every staff prompt below; it is drawn once.
askUntilLegal returns the command and the loop ends.
Polymorphism: performSeating(SeatingStaff, Customer) calls seat() through the SeatingStaff
interface, so the same routine seats for the Host or the Waiter.
Polymorphism: the customer chooses its own food and applies its own discount
(VIPCustomer: 10% off), then the promotion applies 20% off. The price 1080 is
locked in a final field of o4.
A Burger needs one preparation unit, so o4 becomes READY with readyAtTurn = 10.
C4 is ORDERED, so it is still waiting: a VIP loses 5, from 100 to 95.
hasRunOutOfPatience() is then false for everyone, so nobody leaves.
Happy Hour counts down; isActive() is still true, with one turn left.
Turn 11 Step 2: Happy Hour goodwill, then the Waiter serves order #4.
C4 is still waiting for food: 95 + 15 is capped at 100.
Guard: status == READY and readyAtTurn (10) < 11. The same check refuses a dish that
became READY during the current turn.
C4 is now SERVED and loses no more satisfaction. The Host and the Chef have only wait
available this turn, so they are not asked.
Happy Hour has run its 2 turns. NoPromotion charges full price from now on;
Turn 12 Step 4: C4 has eaten for one full turn.
isPayableOn(12) needs readyToPayAtTurn < 12, so a customer who became ready to pay
this turn pays next turn at the earliest.
Turn 13 Step 4: the Cashier settles the bill.
Encapsulation: the price was fixed when o4 was created and has no setter, so the end of
Happy Hour cannot change it. Table 2 is free again.
5 paid >= 4, $88.80 >= $45.00, 83.6 >= 60.0: all three targets are met.
Simplification: display-only calls (showInfo, showTurnEnd), plain getters and look-ups (findCustomer, findOrder, findById), the repeated
capacity checks after the first one, consumeTask() after the Host's, and return values that carry no information are omitted. Every
message shown is a real call in the stage-3 code. Not drawn, so that the diagram can follow C4: C3 finishes eating on turn 10 and pays
$15.00 on turn 11, and C5 arrives on turn 13 and is seated, orders and has its dish prepared that turn.
